custom_widgets.what: pick a neutral area; coefficients are set so it becomes grey (settings becomes 'from image area')

modules.notes: Stored params are only the four channel multipliers + preset index. temperature (K) and tint are GUI-derived via _mul2temp/_temp2mul with the camera matrix; Omalux already reuses that math in omalux/native/engine/white_balance.c (its header still says 'extracted from release-5.6.0'; the defines match 5.6.1). Temperature/tint sit under the section label 'scene illuminant temp' (temperature.c:2144; clicking it cycles the slider colouring mode), but that label is not part of the action path. Temperature: digits 0, ' K', hard 1901..25000, no soft range. Tint: 0.135..2.326, 3 digits, no unit, >1 = green, <1 = magenta. Both defaults are recomputed from the as-shot coefficients (slider_set_default, temperature.c:1661-1662). The 'settings' combobox lists 5 fixed entries then camera presets from data/wb_presets.json; 'finetune' (mired) only appears for presets with tuning steps. The five buttons duplicate combobox entries and are hidden unless the 'button bar' preference is on. Scene-referred default is 'as shot to reference' (camera reference/D65 here; real white balance then done in color calibration). One instance only (IOP_FLAGS_ONE_INSTANCE, temperature.c:262); monochrome sensors show 'white balance disabled for camera'. Channel coefficients live in a collapsible section 'channel coefficients' (temperature.c:2176).

controls.label: input profile
controls.default: per image: embedded ICC / enhanced or standard color matrix (reload_defaults colorin.c:1686); $DEFAULT DT_COLORSPACE_ENHANCED_MATRIX

modules.notes: Both profile comboboxes are filled dynamically: input = image-specific profiles (embedded ICC, camera matrices, standard spaces) plus ICC files from the user's 'in' folder; working = profiles with work_pos > -1 plus user ICC files. They store an enum type plus a filename (DT_COLORSPACE_FILE), so no slider mapping. Params 'intent' and 'blue_mapping' have no GUI control. Always on, no enable button (colorin.c:1688-1689), one instance. Technical module: at most an expert dropdown in Omalux.

custom_widgets.what: pick a neutral area (or AI/auto detection) to estimate the scene illuminant
read-only patch showing the illuminant colour that will be turned into white, next to the 'CCT:' approximate temperature label
'area color mapping' collapsible section: sample an input colour (shown as swatch + L/h/c text) and map it to a target colour; correction mode changes the illuminant
'calibrate with a color checker': drag the four corners of a colour-checker chart overlay on the image, then compute/validate/accept a profile; shows delta E text

image_actions: calibrate with a color checker (recompute, validate, accept)
modules.notes: Notebook action 'page' switches tabs. Tab sliders use section = channel name, so actions are e.g. 'red/input R', 'colorfulness/input G', 'gray/normalize channels'. Channel sliders are hard -2..2, 3 digits, no unit; colorfulness and brightness soft -1..1, gray soft 0..1. Defaults: identity matrix red[0]=green[1]=blue[2]=1 (channelmixerrgb.c:3859). Params x,y (illuminant chromaticity) are shown as LCh hue/chroma via conversion (illum_x/illum_y, not from_params); 'chroma' has format '%' without factor (hard max 100 when format set, then hard max 300). The CAT page visibility depends on adaptation and illuminant (_update_illuminants, channelmixerrgb.c:3175-3292). Section titles: 'area color mapping' (label text built by _area_mapping_section_text) and 'calibrate with a color checker'. Multi-instance is common (a second instance defaults to adaptation 'none (bypass)' and acts as plain channel mixer). For Omalux: temperature (CAT tab) is the natural primary; colorfulness/brightness rows are the creative channel mixer and could be detail; the checker workflow needs on-canvas drawing and is out of scope for sliders. Overlaps with 'white balance' (temperature) in scene-referred workflow.

modules.name: channel mixer
modules.purpose: Old tool that mixes the red, green and blue channels into a chosen output channel, e.g. for black-and-white; replaced by color calibration.
modules.notes: Deprecated (IOP_FLAGS_DEPRECATED, channelmixer.c:145; message 'please use the color calibration module instead'). The three sliders edit red[k]/green[k]/blue[k] for the destination k chosen in the combobox; the combobox itself is not a parameter. Params arrays have 7 entries each (hue, saturation, lightness, red, green, blue, gray); $MIN -1 $MAX 1 in introspection but GUI sliders are -2..2 (3 digits). algorithm_version has no GUI. Has B/W film presets (init_presets). Only for old edits; do not offer in new Omalux UI.

modules.name: color balance rgb
modules.purpose: Modern colour grading: vibrance, saturation, contrast and separate colour tints for shadows, mid-tones and highlights.

custom_widgets.what: each hue slider has a picker quad: pick the opposite colour from the image to neutralise a cast (ctrl+click picks the selected colour)
pickers set the white/grey fulcrum from an image area
'luminance ranges' graph (action 'graph') showing the shadows/mid-tones/highlights weighting curves
quad buttons on the three mask sliders overlay a checkerboard mask preview on the image

modules.notes: Already partially in controls.h: global vibrance, gain/chroma, gain/hue, lift/chroma, lift/hue, offset/luminance. Notebook action 'page'. Section labels (display) vs action sections differ: 'linear chroma grading' -> 'chroma', 'perceptual saturation grading' -> 'saturation', 'perceptual brilliance grading' -> 'brilliance', 'global offset' -> 'offset', 'shadows lift' -> 'lift', 'highlights gain' -> 'gain', 'power' -> 'power'. Global sliders (vibrance, contrast, global chroma/saturation/brilliance, hue shift) have no section. All '%' sliders have |hard max| <= 10 so darktable auto-applies factor 100; set_digits(4) then '%' leaves 2 displayed digits. Hue sliders are stored in degrees (0..360, factor 1). 4 ways tab order is offset, lift, gain, power (not shadows-midtones-highlights). Checkerboard colour/size are preferences, not params. Many presets ('basic colorfulness: ...'). Multi-instance is common for grading.

custom_widgets.what: main editor: a periodic curve over hue with 8 nodes for the selected tab; drag nodes up/down, double-click resets, middle-click toggles the slider view, alt+scroll changes page (action 'graph' with elements red..magenta)
picker on 'node placement' picks a hue from the image and marks it on the graph (ctrl+click for area)
sets the white level from an image area
quad buttons visualise the guided-filter weighting / changed output on the image

modules.notes: By default darktable shows only the graph; the 24 per-colour sliders exist but are visible only with the 'show sliders' preference (then 'options' becomes a 4th notebook tab, colorequal.c:2883-2893). Slider actions are '<tab>/<colour>', e.g. 'saturation/red'. Saturation and brightness store a multiplier 0..2 (1 = unchanged) and display raw*100-100 % (factor 100 via '%' auto rule, offset -100, 2 digits); hue shift is stored and shown in degrees. The 8 colour nodes move with 'node placement' (hue_shift), so 'red' etc. are approximate hue names. Maps very well to an Omalux HSL-style slider list (8 colours x 3 tabs); the graph is optional. Guided-filter options are expert-only. No single primary control: the saturation tab (8 sliders) is the most common use.

modules.name: color zones
modules.purpose: Adjusts lightness, colourfulness or hue of chosen colour (or brightness) ranges by drawing curves.

custom_widgets.what: three curves (lightness/chroma/hue output) over the 'select by' axis; drag nodes, scroll to change, edit-by-area mode; action 'graph' has per-band elements
'show color' marks a picked colour on the graph; 'create curve' builds a curve from a picked area (drag/ctrl+drag/shift+drag)
'display selection' overlays the affected area

modules.notes: Notebook tabs (action 'channel') pick which output curve is edited: lightness, chroma or hue; 'select by' chooses the x axis (default hue). The edit is a curve, not sliders: curve[3][20] nodes (x,y in 0..1), so an Omalux slider mapping would need fixed-node presets (e.g. 8 hue bands) - color equalizer is the better slider target. 'mix' is shown with '%' but no factor (hard range -200..200). 'display selection' is a plain toggle button without an action definition here (unclear if it has a shortcut path). Defaults: two flat nodes per curve, centripetal spline (_reset_parameters colorzones.c:827-841).

modules.notes: Params a_offset, b_offset and unbound have no GUI. Plain sliders, no unit, 2 digits. Lab-based, display-referred.

custom_widgets.what: drawn 24/49-patch chart; click a patch to select it, or use the picker on the 'patch' combobox to select the patch nearest to an image colour

modules.notes: Params are up to 49 source/target Lab patches (num_patches default 24) without $MIN/$MAX; the sliders edit the selected patch and are GUI-converted (relative offsets vs absolute Lab, saturation scales a/b together). Typically filled by darktable-chart/styles, not hand-edited. Not a simple slider module; better exposed via presets only.

No single primary control; all eight are plain sliders (slider colour stops painted from the working/display profile).

modules.notes: Deprecated (IOP_FLAGS_DEPRECATED | IOP_FLAGS_ONE_INSTANCE, colortransfer.c:110; 'better use color mapping module instead'). GUI is only a label: 'this module will be removed in the future and is only here so you can switch it off' (colortransfer.c:406). No controls; params flag/hist/mean/var/n are internal. Omalux: show only the on/off state for legacy edits.
